ashby:9fin:4f7394d3-ee8f-4bb5-99e9-28b9d.summary:
9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

sections.title: About 9fin
paras: We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We are bringing Client Engagement together as a single global function under our Global Head of Client Engagement. We are hiring Regional Directors to lead it on the ground. You will own retention, adoption and growth for your region (EMEA or the Americas), lead a team of Client Engagement Managers across a tiered coverage model, and turn client insight into action across the business.

This is a role for a proven CS or AM leader who wants to scale a function. You will inherit a strong foundation, shape the next stage, and be accountable for commercial outcomes: gross and net revenue retention, product adoption, and the health of our most important client relationships.

sections.title: What You’ll Work On
paras: Every day is different, but here is the kind of work you will lead:

sections.title: Leadership & Team Development
bullets: Lead, coach and develop a regional team of Strategic CEMs, Senior CEMs and Client Engagement Managers across the whole region, and the managers beneath you as the team grows.

Run a tiered coverage model: Strategic CSMs for our most important accounts, Senior CSMs for key accounts, and CSMs for the wider base. Define clear roles, service levels and career paths at each level.
Hire, onboard and train to a rapid growth plan, with a strong bench of internal successors.

ashby:airwallex:16b7b0fd-a514-4c3a-802a-.summary:
Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told…

sections.title: How you’ll make impact
paras: T:0 is building an AI-native accounting platform that helps businesses close the books, reconcile, report, and operate with greater speed and confidence. You’ll own the product direction for T:0’s agentic finance experience, turning real customer pain into a clear roadmap and shipped outcomes.
You’ll work from our San Francisco office three days a week.
bullets: Define how AI-native accounting can help businesses close the books, reconcile, report, and operate with greater speed and confidence.
Lead and develop a high-performing team of Product Managers, creating a culture of ownership, product quality, customer focus, and continuous learning.
Lead product discovery and delivery across engineering, design, data, finance, compliance, and commercial teams.
Translate complex accounting and financial workflows into simple, trusted experiences, balancing AI innovation with deterministic controls, auditability, and accuracy.
Build from first principles in an early-stage environment, using customer insight, product data, and rapid iteration to shape a category that is still being defined.
Own product outcomes from discovery through delivery, using qualitative and quantitative signals to test assumptions and iterate quickly.

sections.title: Essentials
bullets: 8 + years experience leading product strategy and delivery for complex B2B, fintech, accounting, financial infrastructure, or AI products.
A track record of taking ambiguous problems from discovery through launch, with clear ownership of product outcomes.
Strong understanding of financial, accounting, or operational workflows and the customer problems they create.
Experience working closely with engineering and design to build and ship high-quality products.
Strong product judgment, with the ability to balance customer value, technical constraints, business priorities, risk, and regulatory considerations.
Clear, direct communication and the ability to influence senior stakeholders across functions.
Comfort using qualitative and quantitative signals to make decisions, test assumptions, and iterate quickly.

sections.title: Preferred
bullets: Experience building AI-native products, intelligent workflows, automation, or agentic systems.
Experience with accounting software, financial operations, enterprise SaaS, or products serving finance teams.
Experience working in an early-stage or zero-to-one product environment.
Familiarity with the challenges of applying probabilistic AI to workflows that require accuracy, controls, and auditability.
Experience working in fintech, payments, or another regulated industry.

sections.title: You’ll thrive here if
bullets: You're excited by a category that hasn't been won yet, and want to be early enough to shape it.
You're comfortable with ambiguity. Give you a problem, not a prescription, and you'll run with it.
You're comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and moving quickly anyway.
You're not precious about your ideas. You push hard for what you believe in, but you pivot fast when the data says otherwise.
You say what you mean. You're direct, but you lead with respect.
You know when to align and when to just decide. Collaboration isn't a way to avoid accountability.
You ask "why" before jumping to "how."

ashby:amplitude:2bb0f6f7-f335-49ee-89ec-.summary:
Amplitude is the leading AI analytics platform, helping over 5,200 customers—including Atlassian, Burger King, NBCUniversal, and Square—build better products and digital experiences. With powerful AI Agents embedded across our platform, teams can analyze, test, and optimize user experiences faster than ever. Ranked #1 across multiple categories in G2’s Winter 2026 Report, Amplitude is the best-in-class solution for product, data, and marketing teams. Learn more at amplitude.com .

As an organization, we deliver for our customers by living our values. We operate from a place of humility, take ownership of problems and successes, approach challenges with a growth mindset, and put our customers at the center of everything we do.

sections.title: As a Senior Technical Success Manager, Emerging Enterprise, you will:
bullets: Own customer deployment, adoption, and outcomes for a portfolio of 30-40 accounts, from presales through renewal

Lead deployment planning and implementation across your book, e.g.: scoping, deployment plan creation, kickoff meetings, use case alignment, coordination of delivery (e.g. managing internal and partner teams), project reporting
Track and manage risks and issues across active deployments, driving resolution before they impact timelines or outcomes
Monitor portfolio health through AI-augmented signals, engaging proactively to accelerate adoption, drive renewals, and deepen stakeholder engagement

Drive product adoption by running live working sessions, identifying new use cases to expand value over time, and showcasing new platform capabilities with a point of view on how they enable customer growth
Develop and maintain success plans tied to customer goals, tracking milestones and risks from onboarding through renewal
Build and deliver executive business reviews that connect Amplitude usage to measurable business impact, turning adoption into a renewal and expansion story
Partner with Account Executives on renewals and expansion, building the value story, coaching champions, and identifying growth opportunities across your book

sections.title: Critical Skills Profile
bullets: Business Acumen: Understands each customer's business model, growth levers, and priorities. Builds a path to value that connects Amplitude's platform to the outcomes that matter most to the customer.

Technical Fluency: Comfortable with Amplitude data architecture, instrumentation methods, taxonomy design, and AI agent workflows. Able to unlock use cases and guide internal and partner delivery teams.

Delivery Excellence: Drives deployment and implementation quality across a full book of business. Manages timelines, coordinates internal and partner delivery teams, and ensures every account progresses through milestones on time and to standard.

Prescriptive Customer Guidance: Sets the standard for what good looks like at each stage of the customer journey. Drives accountability across deployment and ongoing success. Pushes back on bad implementation patterns, guides customers toward proven approaches, and holds them accountable to their own defined success criteria.
Diagnostic Thinking: Proactively recognizes adoption gaps and technical blockers early and drives creative solutions that get customers back on track.

Curiosity and Self-Sufficiency: Defaults to figuring things out independently. Explores edge cases on your own, and comes to conversations with a point of view. This role requires someone who runs toward ambiguity.
AI Innovation: Embeds AI in day-to-day workflow to improve efficiency and customer outcomes. Experiments, iterates, and shares best practices.

sections.title: At a minimum, you need to have:
bullets: 5+ years of experience in Customer Success, Technical Account Management, or a similar customer-facing role in B2B SaaS
2+ years of experience specifically leading enterprise software deployments where change management and foundational data governance were core priorities.
2+ years managing a portfolio of 20+ mid-market or emerging enterprise accounts
Experience co-owning renewals and contributing to expansion pipeline alongside a sales counterpart
Experience training or enabling non-technical teams to become data-sufficient.
Excellent communication skills to influence everyone from a data engineer to a C-level executive.
Expert-level project management skills and the ability to thrive in an independent and fast-paced environment.

ashby:apollo-graphql:f3c918e6-ac7f-4d9f-.summary:
At Apollo GraphQL, we’re on a mission to make it radically easier for engineering teams to ship fast, reliable products and services on top of the world’s data, powering everything from web to mobile to agentic experiences..

We’re looking for a Senior Solution Engineer who loves stepping into business‑critical challenges and turning them into clear, elegant architectures that customers can’t wait to build. As a Senior SE, you’ll be the technical quarterback on some of our most important opportunities: partnering with prospects and customers to design and scale their supergraph on GraphOS, and helping them prove out real impact in production.

sections.title: What you’ll do
bullets: Own complex technical evaluations for strategic new and existing accounts: lead discovery, workshops, and solution design to deeply understand customer APIs, architectures, and constraints, and turn them into clear required capabilities and technical win plans.

Design and present multi‑system solution architectures that show how Apollo’s supergraph, GraphOS, and tooling fit into modern cloud‑native environments —meeting customers where they are while charting a safe, future‑proof path forward.

Lead compelling, value‑focused demos and PoCs , translating complex technical capabilities into simple, business‑aligned stories for audiences ranging from lead developers and architects to VP/C‑suite decision makers.

De‑risk and win complex deals by anticipating and resolving technical blockers (security, compliance, integration, performance), building customer confidence that Apollo will work in their environment, and partnering with AEs on value‑based selling, and close strategy.

Partner tightly with Sales, CS, Product, and Engineering : act as a trusted advisor throughout the account lifecycle, feed structured field insight back into roadmap and positioning, and contribute reusable reference architectures, playbooks, and patterns that the broader team can use at scale.

Elevate the team through enablement and AI‑augmented workflows : mentor junior SEs, share best practices, and actively use AI tooling (including agentic/MCP‑based workflows) to improve discovery, architecture design, and demo/PoC execution.

sections.title: Who you are
paras: You’re an experienced, hands‑on Solutions Engineer (or architect in a similar customer‑facing role) who loves sitting at the intersection of code, architecture, and commercial impact. You’re just as comfortable whiteboarding a distributed system with staff engineers as you are explaining the “so what?” to a VP of Engineering or CIO, and you thrive when you can roll up your sleeves on a PoC, earn technical trust, and guide a customer from “evaluation” to “we can’t imagine building without this.”

You see Solutions Engineering as part of the go‑to‑market engine: your purpose is not just to “be technical” but to help progress qualified opportunities toward successful outcomes—new ARR, healthy renewals, and meaningful expansions.

sections.title: Minimum requirements
bullets: 4+ years in a pre‑sales Solutions Engineering or equivalent technical customer‑facing role (sales engineer, field engineer, customer engineer, or architect) working on complex B2B SaaS or infrastructure products.

Deep domain expertise around APIs and integration , with prior experience working both with teams who build APIs and with teams who consume them, integrating into existing architectures and tool stacks (CI/CD, observability, cloud, API gateways, etc.).

Strong architecture and integration skills across modern web/cloud stacks —comfortable discussing REST/GraphQL, microservices, identity/security, and data flows, and designing multi‑system architectures that can be implemented in real‑world environments.

Proven track record owning complex technical evaluations end‑to‑end , including discovery, solution design, PoC implementation guidance, objection handling, and technical win for enterprise or upper‑mid‑market accounts.

Executive‑level communication and storytelling skills : able to move fluidly between deep technical detail and clear business value for developers, architects, product leaders, and executives, and to act as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders.
Sales process and value‑based selling fluency : comfortable with MEDDPICC, team selling with AEs/CS, and framing Apollo’s capabilities in terms of commercial impact.
Collaborative, low‑ego teammate who works well across Sales, Product, Engineering, and CS, mentors less‑tenured SEs, and prefers creating reusable assets over one‑off work.

sections.title: Nice to have
bullets: Hands‑on GraphQL experience , ideally including schema design, federation, or operating production GraphQL services—whether from a previous SE role, as an engineer, or through meaningful side projects.
Background as a software engineer or architect , with the ability to read code, reason about performance and scalability trade‑offs, and pair productively with customer engineering teams.
Experience selling or implementing developer‑focused platforms (APIs, integration platforms, data/analytics, observability, or adjacent infra) into large or regulated enterprises.
Familiarity with common security, compliance, and networking topics that come up in enterprise evaluations (SSO, RBAC, data residency, SOC 2, VPC/networking patterns).

Comfort in fast‑moving, high‑growth environments , where you help shape the playbook (including via AI/agentic tooling) rather than just follow it, and enjoy contributing to content, enablement, and broader GTM strategy.

ashby:applied:f9926b5d-475a-42cc-bd6e-f3.summary: Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co .

sections.title: About the role
paras: Data Engine powers the data workflows behind Applied Intuition's autonomy programs across Cars, Trucks, Industrials, and Defense. We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to make it a coherent platform that technical teams can discover, adopt, and rely on—from bringing data into the system to producing useful, traceable datasets.

Your first customers are the engineers and researchers building autonomy inside Applied. You will work directly with them to understand how they get work done, identify where shared capabilities can replace duplicated effort, and turn their needs into a clear product strategy. Your responsibility extends across ingestion, processing, data discovery, enrichment, quality, and dataset delivery—not just the boundaries of a single engineering team.

You will also own the external product roadmap, customer discovery, and packaging for this platform, working with commercial partners on pricing and go-to-market. You will determine what transfers to external customers and what additional deployment, onboarding, and support capabilities they need.

sections.title: At Applied Intuition, you will
bullets: Own the end-to-end product. Set the vision, roadmap, and priorities across multiple teams behind our Data Engine. Define the workflows we support, their users, and what a reliable production experience requires.

Stay close to users. Observe real workflows, interview users and non-users, investigate workarounds, and combine that evidence with usage and support signals. Make sure teams understand what happened to their feedback and why.

Build shared capabilities without erasing real differences. Decide what belongs in the common platform, what needs configuration or extension points, and what should remain program-specific. Make explicit choices about what not to build.

Own adoption beyond launch. Partner with design and engineering on APIs, interfaces, documentation, examples, onboarding, and migrations. Help users find existing capabilities and retire duplicated implementations when the shared path is ready.

Make technical tradeoffs with engineering. Translate user needs into clear requirements and acceptance criteria. Balance reliability, data quality, latency, cost, compatibility, and delivery speed while respecting security and data-residency constraints.

Connect internal and external needs. Lead external discovery, define a repeatable offering and its limits, and build a commercial roadmap with sales and customer-facing partners. Avoid turning individual customer requests into permanent product forks.

Measure outcomes and communicate decisions. Track workflow success, onboarding time, adoption, support effort, and reuse. Explain priorities, tradeoffs, and risks clearly to program teams and leadership.

sections.title: We're looking for someone who has
bullets: MS/BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
4+ years of Product Management experience at a top tech company or high-growth startup
A record of owning complex technical products from discovery through delivery, adoption, and iteration, with senior-level responsibility for decisions and results.
Experience serving technical users through a shared platform, developer product, or data/ML product, including reconciling competing needs across multiple teams or customers.
Strong discovery skills: you can distinguish a requested feature from the underlying problem and show how user evidence changed a product decision.
Sound platform judgment: you can balance reuse with necessary specialization, set support boundaries, and sequence migration without blocking users' work.
Technical fluency in data flows, APIs, workflow orchestration, data quality, and production operations. You can discuss architectural tradeoffs with engineers.

sections.title: Nice to have
paras: Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
bullets: Experience with autonomy, robotics, sensor data, or other physical AI workflows.
Experience with ingestion, catalogs and lineage, data processing, ML data pipelines, or workflow orchestration.
Experience converting an internal platform into an external product, or supporting customer-controlled and multi-region deployments.
Prior software engineering experience or hands-on work with technical users, APIs, and developer tooling.

ashby:arq:42bfc312-fb18-43aa-95a3-b3b98a.summary: ARQ is one of the fastest-growing fintechs in the world. Our mission is to redefine how people interact with money across borders, building the infrastructure to move value seamlessly. We're still early in our journey, which means every person who joins shapes the future of our product, culture, and growth. If you're excited by big challenges, global impact, and the chance to grow fast with a world-class team, ARQ is the place to do it.

sections.title: The Role
paras: We're hiring a Product Owner to build and own ARQ's operating system: the company-wide KPI platform, the employee directory it runs on, and the back-office tools that let ARQ grow and stay efficient. ARQ barely pays for external software anymore. The systems we run on are the ones we build ourselves, and this role owns them.

You'll work directly with the founders, engineers, and department leads across the company. The mandate isn't to patch together basic internal tools. It's to own the platforms that ARQ runs on end-to-end.

sections.title: What you'll be doing
bullets: Owning the product strategy, roadmap, and execution of ARQ's operating system end-to-end.
Shipping the company-wide KPI platform that the founders, board, and every department use to run ARQ.
Building out the employee directory: profiles, org chart, people-to-KPI attribution, integration with our HR stack.
Driving department leads across the company to define, commit to, and report against the KPIs that matter for their area.
Partnering with back-office engineering on schema and architecture decisions to make the platforms scale together.
Tracking adoption and usage, iterating fast based on internal feedback.

sections.title: What you'll need
bullets: 2 to 5 years of experience with 2+ years experience at a top technology company.
A founder's mindset: a problem solver ready to roll up their sleeves to build from scratch.
Strong analytical and quantitative skills; comfortable going deep into data and processes.
Excellent written communicator. Confident working directly with founders and cross-functional stakeholders.
A self-starter who thrives in ambiguity and takes full ownership.

sections.title: Nice-to-haves
bullets: Experience building internal tools, BI platforms, or HR-tech products.
Familiarity with metrics frameworks, dashboards, or org-data products.
Spanish or Portuguese language skills.

ashby:ashby:2b401986-a491-4f9b-9c22-6307.summary:

sections.title: About Ashby

ashby:away:441140c4-ceb6-4998-a27a-a288e.summary: We believe travel makes us better. Launched in 2016 with one perfectly designed carry-on, we now offer a range of luggage and travel essentials for every journey. ashby:beam-up:15252bbe-8651-445e-b1f2-37.summary:
At Beam, we’re building AI that serves society.

We're a global team of ambitious, hardworking problem solvers, applying fast-moving startup energy to work that makes the world a better place. If you want to apply your talent to the biggest problems society faces, Beam is the place for you.

You’ll be part of a high-performance culture where you'll make a huge impact, rapidly progress your career, and truly enjoy your work.

Over 120,000 frontline workers across 400+ customers already use Beam to take notes, provide live interpretation and handle phone calls, so they can focus on the people who need them most. This is just the beginning.

sections.title: About the role:
paras: As one of Beam’s first Account Managers in the US, you’ll take the customers our sales team wins and grow them into our biggest partnerships. You’ll work closely with senior leadership while the team is still small enough that your results shape how Beam grows across the US.

Our US customers are counties and states, and you’ll be their trusted partner at the senior level. You’ll find where else Beam can help, and build the relationships that make leaders want to work with us again. Every account you grow puts Beam in front of more frontline workers, and gives them more time for the people who need them.
This role is fully remote, and candidates must currently live in Central or Eastern Time Zone. Please submit one application for the Account Manager opening that matches your current time zone.

sections.title: You’ll Be:
bullets: Owning Your Book: Managing a portfolio of around $1m to $2m, with deals typically between $100k and $150k and a growing number above $200k.
Converting and Expanding: Converting pilots to subscriptions, then growing them into multi-team, multi-product partnerships across new service areas.
Building Senior Relationships: Working with economic buyers, division directors and IT leaders, and turning them into champions who join us at conferences and webinars.

Navigating Public Funding: Understanding how state and county budgets work so you can position Beam well within them.
Representing Beam in Your States: Becoming a driving force behind our reputation and visibility across a number of states in the US.
Working Closely with Colleagues: Partnering with customer success, sales and product so customers get a joined-up experience where our learnings shape what we build next.

sections.title: You Have:
bullets: A Record of Growing Accounts: 3+ years in account management or full-cycle sales, with proven success expanding customer relationships and closing large deals, ideally in B2B SaaS and with a book of a similar size.
Senior-Level Presence: Experience selling to senior stakeholders, and the confidence to be consultative rather than scripted.
Energy and Sharpness: You’re curious and quick, and you ask real questions that come out of the conversation, not just ones you’d planned to run through.
A Habit of Experimenting: You test ideas, learn from what lands, and continuously iterate upon them.
Complex Deal Experience: Comfort with long buying journeys involving procurement, legal and several decision-makers.
Startup Pace: The drive to work at speed in an early-stage team, where you’ll help define the role as you go.
Public Sector Curiosity (Nice to Have): Experience in government, public sector or social care is helpful but not essential. We’ll teach you the rest.

sections.title: Success looks like:
bullets: Pilots in your accounts converting to subscriptions, with ARR growing quarter-on-quarter
Expansion into new service areas and multi-product partnerships within your accounts
A pipeline of expansion opportunities that you’ve identified and built yourself
Senior champions in each account who advocate for Beam and work with us as partners
Beam’s reputation and visibility growing in your states
Contracts, procurement and legal handled smoothly and on time

ashby:certifyos:cc684b29-ff63-4246-a04a-.summary:

ashby:meridianlink:b7d0d877-bea3-4b39-96.summary:
We are looking for a Product Manager to define and deliver an AI assistant inside our lending and account-opening products. Users will ask questions in plain language, get accurate answers grounded in product and institution knowledge, and take action without leaving their workflow.

This is an early-stage product area. Choosing the right use cases, and the right quality bar, is the job. You will find where an assistant genuinely beats search, documentation, and a support call, and where it does not, then take the best opportunities to production on our shared AI platform.

You have shipped LLM-powered features to external customers, not just prototypes, and you care about answers that are accurate, grounded in sources, and honest about what they cannot do.

sections.title: Product Strategy and Roadmap
bullets: Define the product vision and roadmap for assistant experiences across lending and account-opening products.

Work with product teams to identify and prioritize use cases (for example product guidance, knowledge retrieval, natural-language questions about data and reports, and guided actions) by user value, feasibility, and risk.
Build business cases and success metrics for each use case before investing.
Evaluate build, buy, and partner options for core components and make the tradeoffs visible.

sections.title: Discovery and Customer Engagement
bullets: Research the top questions and tasks of loan officers, processors, institution staff, and end customers, and validate that an assistant beats existing self-serve and support options.
Work with design partners and early-access customers to test and refine assistant behavior.
Synthesize qualitative research, usage data, and support data into clear opportunities.

bullets: Partner closely with the AI platform team on shared capabilities such as retrieval, tool access, guardrails, and observability, and shape what the platform needs to support.
Work with engineering, design, and data science teams using agile practices to define requirements, acceptance criteria, and the evaluation approach.
Define how quality is measured before and after launch: answer accuracy, groundedness, task completion, and when to hand off to a human.
Work with support, documentation, and content owners so the knowledge behind the assistant stays accurate and current.
Coordinate with security, privacy, legal, and compliance on data access, permissions, disclosures, and regulatory expectations for AI in financial services.
Own launch readiness: go-to-market coordination, documentation, training, and customer communication.

sections.title: Measurement and Iteration
bullets: Track KPIs such as answer quality, resolution and deflection rate, task completion, adoption, escalation rate, and cost per conversation.
Build feedback mechanisms that surface wrong or unhelpful answers quickly and feed them into iteration cycles.
Communicate performance transparently to leadership and stakeholders.

ashby:owner:29efc81c-acaa-437b-8d7f-f203.summary:
About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.

Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.

sections.title: Our vision
paras: We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.

But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.
Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.

sections.title: Our traction
paras: Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com website.
More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.

sections.title: Our team

We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.

ashby:pivotal-health:f51dcac5-1d09-49a3-.summary:
Pivotal Health is the leading technology platform that helps healthcare providers get paid fairly in an increasingly complex reimbursement landscape.

Today, many providers face persistent underpayment from health insurance companies, despite delivering high-quality care. While processes like IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) were designed to promote fairness, they’re often administrative-heavy, time-consuming, and difficult to navigate without the right tools.

Pivotal Health combines software, data, and service into a seamlessly integrated, AI-driven platform that simplifies these complex reimbursement workflows. We help providers efficiently dispute underpaid claims, reduce administrative burden, and recover the reimbursement they’re entitled to; without adding more work to already stretched teams.

sections.title: About Pivotal Health
paras: Our full-service IDR solution is just the starting point. We’re building solutions that enable providers to operate with clarity, control, and confidence across the reimbursement journey.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We're hiring a Product Manager to join Pivotal's Case Execution team and help build the systems that move eligible healthcare claims through the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process. You'll partner closely with product, operations, and engineering to improve core workflows across eligibility, claim batching, negotiation, and arbitration, helping more claims reach resolution and improving outcomes for healthcare providers.

This is a strong fit for someone who enjoys investigating complex problems, working directly with data, and owning initiatives from discovery through launch and measurement. Your work will span federal and state arbitration workflows, with opportunities to uncover operational challenges, identify where technology can make the greatest impact, and deliver practical solutions. You'll learn from an experienced product leader while taking ownership of defined initiatives, with room to grow into a dedicated product area and engineering partnership.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Own product initiatives from discovery through delivery: Investigate problems, define requirements, prioritize solutions, and partner with engineering to launch improvements. Measure results and drive further iteration.

Understand and improve case execution workflows: Work closely with operations to understand how claims move through federal and state IDR processes. Identify manual steps, exceptions, bottlenecks, and processes that need to evolve as the business scales.

Use data to guide product decisions: Write SQL queries, learn our data models, and conduct your own analysis to understand claim funnel performance, quantify opportunities, and evaluate the impact of product changes.

Turn complex problems into clear product direction: Distill stakeholder input, operational details, and analytical findings into focused problem statements, actionable requirements, and clear measures of success.

Prioritize practical, incremental solutions: Break large problems into manageable releases, weigh business impact against effort, and make thoughtful tradeoffs as priorities shift across federal and state workflows.

Drive progress across teams: Align product, operations, and engineering on decisions, dependencies, and next steps. Communicate clearly, surface blockers early, and keep initiatives moving through consistent follow-through.

Strong SQL skills, with the ability to independently query data, investigate unfamiliar tables, validate findings, and use analysis to inform decisions

ashby:simpleclosure:7341c7b1-f2dc-42dd-b.summary:
Most companies don’t end in acquisition — they end in closure. Yet shutdown has never been given the same rigor, clarity, or professionalism as the moments that came before it. Nearly 4 million companies shut down every year, creating a massive, overlooked market. SimpleClosure is building the infrastructure to change that.

Having raised over $20M from leading VCs and trusted by more than 7,000 companies to date, we streamline the entire business dissolution process — from legal and tax to operational and administrative — as one coordinated effort instead of a patchwork of disconnected steps. We go a step further, helping companies sell their remaining assets and return the most value to their stakeholders, through our AssetHub.

sections.title: Company Overview
paras: As the leading platform for company shutdowns, we have something no one else does: a continuous, proprietary flow of companies winding down, and the assets they built along the way. Our buyers span the top AI labs, RL environment providers, vertical and enterprise agent builders, VCs and deal-flow partners, domain marketplaces, and much more. Dissolution is our wedge; the marketplace is a big part of where we’re headed.

Joining our AssetHub team means helping to define a new category from the ground up, working on complex, high-stakes problems, and building the products and processes that guide founders through one of the most consequential moments in a company’s life.

sections.title: Job Overview
paras: SimpleClosure is seeking a Customer Success Manager to secure the rights to the assets that power AssetHub and deliver them to our AI buyers. When a company shuts down, the codebases, workspaces, and proprietary data it built can be worth a lot, but only if the rights are clean. You will work directly with founders, investors, and counsel at companies selling their assets, negotiate and close the deals, and then own delivery to buyers such as top AI labs, RL environment providers, and agent builders. This is a short-cycle, high-ownership sales/customer success role: you will run many deals at once, from first conversation to signed agreement to delivered asset.

We are a legal tech company at heart. We buy assets from sellers and license them to buyers, and we care about the rights and risks of every party involved. Our position in the market is a curated selection of high-quality assets that come with the rights and the data to back them up. Your job is to select great assets, secure those rights on terms that are economical for us and responsible for sellers and buyers, and make sure every deal is one both sides can stand behind. You will also pass what you learn back to the team, so we can keep structuring the marketplace in a way where buyers and sellers both win.
*This is a fully remote role, open to candidates anywhere in the U.S.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Own the supply-side deal cycle from first conversation to signed agreement: qualify sellers and assets, position Asset Hub clearly, negotiate, and close the rights to codebases, workspaces, and other assets.
Build trust with founders, boards, and investors by explaining clearly how licensing works, what rights we are acquiring, and how the process protects them.

Negotiate agreements in close partnership with legal, and responsibly adjust our contracts deal by deal, using sound judgment on which terms we can and cannot give (scope of rights, exclusivity, reps and warranties, and payment structure).

Help select the right assets: weigh quality, buyer demand, and rights clarity, and flag legal, IP, privacy, and third-party risks early, so every asset we take on is one we can license with confidence.

Own delivery: carry each asset from signed deal to delivered product for our AI buyers, coordinating with engineering, legal, and operations on transfer, packaging, de-identification, and buyer acceptance.
Keep deals moving: manage a high-volume pipeline in HubSpot, forecast accurately, and keep sellers and buyers informed at every step.

Be the voice of the market inside the team: share what you hear from sellers and buyers on terms, pricing, and process, so product, legal, and the GM of Asset Hub can structure the marketplace in a way that works for everyone.
Build repeatable playbooks, templates, and workflows (using AI tools where they help) that make each deal faster and more consistent than the last.

sections.title: Desired Skills & Qualifications
bullets: Sales and negotiation (critical): a track record of closing deals through strong positioning and negotiation, ideally in a short-cycle, high-volume environment. You know how to read a counterparty, hold a position, and find the structure that works for both sides.
Experience: 2-4 years in sales, customer success, deal-making, or a similar commercial role, ideally involving contracts, IP or data licensing, M&A, regulatory environments or marketplaces.

Working with legal: comfortable reading and marking up agreements, partnering with counsel, and responsibly adjusting terms. You do not need to be a lawyer, but you understand rights, licensing, and risk well enough to know what we can and cannot offer.
Strategic judgment: you think beyond the single deal: which terms are worth giving, which are not, and what each concession means for sellers, buyers, and how we structure the marketplace.
Ownership: goal-oriented, entrepreneurial, and flexible. You take a deal from first call to delivered asset, and you thrive in a brand-new market where the playbook is still being written.
Communication: a clear, credible communicator who can earn trust quickly with founders, investors, counsel, and technical buyers.
Operational rigor: organized enough to run many deals at once, keep a clean pipeline, and coordinate delivery across legal, engineering, and operations. Comfortable using AI tools to move faster.
Nice to have: experience in M&A, asset sales, IP or data licensing, legal tech, or the startup wind-down ecosystem; familiarity with software, data, or the AI training landscape.

Tu es un team player (Succeed as One) : tu crées un alignement tôt avec le Produit et les Sales, tu partages l'info sans qu'on te la demande, tu participes activement aux problèmes cross-team , et tu sais que c'est le résultat collectif qui compte

Tu es Curious to the Core : tu questionnes avant d'exécuter, tu remets en question le statu quo lorsque nécessaire et tu restes curieux·se face aux nouveaux outils dont l'IA, aux autres équipes et à notre industrie
Tu choisis Booxi : notre mission, notre marché et ce que ça veut dire de construire dans une scale-up

sections.title: TON PROFIL
bullets: 6+ ans d'expérience en B2B, dont une bonne part à comprendre un marché et à le raconter : product marketing, conseil, recherche ou analyse. Ton titre compte moins que ce que tu as fait bouger

Tu as déjà fait évoluer un positionnement ou un message avec ce que tu entendais sur le terrain, et tu l'as fait tenir dans la durée

bamboohr:dnastack:37.summary:
At DNAstack , our mission is to power precision medicine by building software that breaks down barriers to responsible biomedical data sharing, discovery, and analysis. We build cutting-edge software and industry standards to help researchers and clinicians analyze sequencing data and make faster, more accurate diagnoses. Our platform supports national and international networks tackling rare disease, cancer, infectious disease, and more.

We’re a nimble, cross-functional team of scientists, engineers, designers, and product thinkers working at the intersection of genomics, software, and cloud technologies. Our mission is ambitious, and so is our team.

sections.title: From the job description
paras: The Bioinformatics Customer Success Specialist makes sure every customer gets accurate, timely, and dependable results from the DNAstack platform. You are the technical owner of the customer experience after go-live: the first responder when a run fails, the person who confirms a result is right before it ships, and the voice that brings customer pain points back to engineering and product.

This is a growth-oriented role for an M.S.-level bioinformatician who enjoys both the science and the people. You will start on the front line of our operations: resolving support tickets, monitoring production pipelines across AWS and GCP, running and validating sample batches, and preparing custom deliverables for partners. That work gives you an intimate view of our architecture and of what customers actually need.

As your expertise grows, you will move from fixing issues to preventing them. You will build quality checks and regression tests, benchmark new tools against reference standards, maintain pipeline dependencies, and help set the reliability standards that our clinical and research customers depend on.
3. Customer Onboarding and Data Operations
bullets: Serve as the primary technical point of contact for customer support tickets, partner inquiries, and data delivery requests.
Triage, diagnose, and resolve failed secondary and tertiary pipeline runs, annotation and sorting bugs, and cloud permission issues within agreed response times.
Lead root-cause investigations into missing variants, control sample mismatches (e.g., commercial reference controls), and runtime bottlenecks, and communicate findings clearly to customers.
Turn recurring issues into knowledge-base articles, runbooks, and FAQs so customers and teammates can self-serve.
Monitor production workflows and dataset deployments across GCP and AWS, catching failures and performance drift before customers notice.
Define and run quality-control checks on pipeline inputs and outputs, including sample identity, coverage, and variant-level QC metrics.
Run regression and validation tests on new pipeline and platform releases using reference materials (e.g., GIAB) before they reach customers.

Estimate and track workflow compute costs across cloud platforms, giving internal teams and customers realistic cost ranges for workflows and versions and informing selection of preferred cloud when onboarding new customers.

500,000+ customers. 175 countries. Nasdaq: BLZE. backblaze.com

sections.title: The Role

Nearly every customer is replacing something they already run. Your job is to show where Backblaze slots into what they have already built, not to design their stack from scratch. You will earn trust by being curious, hands-on, and straight with customers about what the test shows.
This is not a demo-and-handoff role. If your instinct is to open a terminal, test a customer's real workload, and write down what you find, keep reading.

Hand off cleanly. Take the lead through the technical win, then step back so the AE can carry the deal through negotiation.
Stay engaged after the sale. Answer questions in shared customer channels, help customers adopt the platform, and work with the AE on expansion.
Carry the field back to Product. Capture gaps and requests with evidence.
Share what you learn. Contribute benchmarks, technical content, and events.

sections.title: What We Are Looking For
bullets: Curiosity. You dig into technical workflows and pick apart what customers tell you. This is the trait that matters most.
Programming fluency. You are comfortable in at least one language, any language, and use it to script tests and automate work.
Customer-facing experience. You have worked directly with customers in solutions engineering, support, technical account management, consulting, or a similar role. A sales background is not required.

Working knowledge of cloud infrastructure. You can explain how compute, storage, and networking fit into an AI data pipeline and where a storage layer sits. Experience on any cloud counts, whether AWS, Google, Azure, or CoreWeave. You don't need to have built these systems yourself.
Strong communication. You can explain a technical result clearly to an engineer or an executive, and you listen well.

Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

sections.title: THE ROLE
paras: Shape the future of enterprise infrastructure by leading product strategy for Fusion, the intelligent control plane at the heart of Everpure’s Enterprise Data Cloud. Rather than leaving teams to manually configure individual storage systems, you will empower global enterprises to define high-level intent while Fusion autonomously governs, optimizes, and protects their entire data estate. Operating with wide strategic latitude, you will partner across FlashArray, FlashBlade, platform engineering, architecture, and enterprise customers to turn next-generation control plane concepts into industry-defining products.

sections.title: WHAT YOU'LL DO
bullets: Shape Fusion’s Control Plane Strategy and Execution: Exercise wide latitude to define product vision, architectural tradeoffs, and roadmap priorities for core Fusion capabilities, partnering with engineering and architecture teams to deliver scalable, zero-friction operating experiences for enterprise IT leaders.

Pioneer Policy-Driven Operations and Continuous Compliance: Design intuitive policy engines, configuration drift detection, and automated remediation workflows with platform engineering so customers can standardize service levels and measurably reduce operational risk across their infrastructure.

Deliver Intelligent Placement and Autonomous Optimization: Partner with engineering and data science teams to build dynamic workload rebalancing and verifiable automation safeguards, improving fleet-wide capacity and performance utilization while upholding strict customer-defined service levels.

Unify Multi-Protocol and AI-Ready Platform Abstractions: Collaborate across FlashArray, FlashBlade, and ecosystem teams to extend consistent APIs, orchestration, and agentic management workflows across block, file, and object storage—simplifying hybrid cloud operations for infrastructure architects.

Accelerate Enterprise Adoption and Product Impact: Build formal networks with key customer decision-makers and serve as an external product spokesperson, partnering with sales, solutions architecture, and customer success to drive measurable growth in policy utilization, workload coverage, and automation adoption.

greenhouse:scotch:5435689008.summary:
Scotch is building the next-generation operating system for beverage alcohol retailers — combining POS, payments, back office, and e-commerce into a platform purpose-built for liquor stores.

We’re modernizing one of the oldest industries in the world: the $1.6T beverage alcohol market. Our platform helps retailers run more efficiently through streamlined payments, inventory management, reporting, and day-to-day operations.

Our founders came from Skupos (acquired 2023) and Drizly (acquired by Uber). We've raised $28M from VMG Partners, First Round, Lerer Hippeau, Watchfire, and Toba Capital, with angels including the founder of Drizly and early Toast executives. Forbes has recognized Scotch as a leader in liquor retail tech. We closed a $20M Series A in 2026 off 500%+ YoY growth and $1B+ in processed payment volume.

sections.title: Position Overview
paras: We're looking for a Product Manager to own the in-store experience at Scotch — the Android point-of-sale terminal our merchants use to ring up every sale. It's the part of our product customers touch every day, and it's where we're most visibly right or wrong.

This is a hands-on role with real autonomy. You'll own the terminal end-to-end: spending time in stores watching people use it, setting direction for what we build, and working with engineering to ship it. You'll be the person who knows how the device actually behaves in a busy store on a Friday night, not just how it behaves in a demo.

We're a small product org. That means you'll make calls without a committee, and you'll be accountable for the ones that turn out wrong. You won't be setting strategy alone — but you'll have a real hand in shaping it, and the closest view of the customer of anyone in the room.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Own the roadmap for our point-of-sale app. Shape the direction for the register experience with us, turn it into a sequence of releases, and defend the tradeoffs to people who'd rather ship something else.

Prioritize across merchant escalations, platform work, and the long-horizon bets that never feel urgent. Partner closely with engineering on scoping and sequencing, including the parts where the right answer is "not yet."
Spend real time in stores with merchants and their staff. Learn what they need, what they actually do, and where those two differ, and bring back things nobody would have found in a ticket.

Translate messy, conflicting merchant input into a clear direction, and hold that direction when the inputs keep changing. Write requirements that describe the problem and the outcome, not the implementation.
Make sure the app holds up in a real store: the peripherals it talks to, the network it doesn't always have, and the pace it has to keep up with.

Own releases end to end. Decide what ships and what waits, how it rolls out, and who needs to know before it lands. Own the response when something goes wrong on a device that's already sitting on a counter.

Serve as the product point of contact for support, onboarding, and go-to-market on anything happening at the register. That includes writing the release notes that keep those teams ahead of what's shipping, and eventually getting them in front of merchants too.
Define what success looks like before we build, then go look. Instrument the work, watch adoption, and say plainly when something didn't land.

sections.title: Qualifications & Skills
bullets: 5+ years of product management experience.
A track record of being the only person accountable for a decision, with no one reviewing your work before it shipped. This matters more to us than company size or whether you've worked at a startup.

A consistent habit of direct customer contact. You've sat with users, watched them work, and changed your mind because of what you saw. In this role, that happens in person at merchants' stores, not over video calls.
Sound judgment you can explain. You can walk through a call you got wrong, ideally one you caught yourself before anyone pointed it out.
Experience running several workstreams at once and making the tradeoffs between them yourself, not only executing on priorities someone else set.
Clear communication for different audiences. You can write a spec an engineer can build from, then explain the same decision to a merchant, a support lead, and an executive.

sections.title: Nice to Haves
bullets: Experience with hardware, peripherals, or devices deployed in the field — printers, scanners, card readers, or anything that fails in ways software alone doesn't
Products built for environments where the user is busy, interrupted, and has a customer waiting
Retail or point-of-sale background, particularly with independent or small-format merchants
Payments experience — tender types, reconciliation, or dual pricing
Fluency with AI tools in your daily workflow

bullets: Kubernetes operator: Making Tailscale a natural part of Kubernetes infrastructure, enabling secure connectivity to and from clusters.
Ephemeral workloads: Enabling CI/CD runners, containers, and automated jobs to securely connect at scale.
Agent connectivity: Enabling AI agents to securely connect to the tools, services, and private infrastructure they need to operate.
Cloud and infrastructure integrations: Making Tailscale easy to deploy and operate within the cloud platforms and infrastructure tools developers already use.
Workload Connectivity as a business: Defining how machine-to-machine connectivity is packaged, measured, and monetized independently of traditional user-based VPN subscriptions.

sections.title: Work Personas
paras: We approach our distributed world of work with flexibility and trust. Work personas (flexible, remote, or required in office) are categories that are assigned to ServiceNow employees depending on the nature of their work and their assigned work location. Learn more here . To determine eligibility for a work persona, ServiceNow may confirm the distance between your primary residence and the closest ServiceNow office using a third-party service.
